title: Verifier-integrated LLM intent→configuration pipeline: an artifact-grounded paired evaluation and lessons from a ceiling effect
abstract: We preregistered (CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001) and executed a paired experiment to test whether inserting an automated network verifier (block-on-violation) into an LLM-driven intent→configuration pipeline reduces unsafe enactments. Using a shared-initial generation policy with gpt-5-mini on 150 paired intents (300 episodes), both the baseline (LLM-only) and guarded (LLM+verifier-block) pipelines produced identical, verifier-accepted candidates in every episode (n11=150, n10=n01=n00=0). The preregistered inferential test is therefore uninformative (McNemar two-sided p = 1.0); paired-bootstrap 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). We release the complete artifact bundle (preregistration, execution manifest, provider-call traces, per-episode scoring JSONs, response transcripts, and SHA256 hashes), diagnose why a ceiling effect occurred (shared-initial generation + verifier acceptance predicates), document the untestability of the preregistered rollback hypothesis, and give artifact-grounded prescriptions for future verifier evaluations designed to produce informative discordant outcomes.

sections.introduction: Intent-driven network configuration maps operator intent (natural language) to device-level commands. For operational NetOps the central assurance question is whether generation-plus-validation architectures materially reduce enactment risk compared to unguided generation. We preregistered CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001 to evaluate two confirmatory hypotheses in a paired design: H1—LLM+verifier-block reduces the per-task unsafe-enactment rate relative to LLM-only; H2—verifier-detected violations that trigger automated rollback reduce end-to-end service impact compared to LLM-only. The preregistration and all artifacts were frozen before execution. After execution we observed a deterministic ceiling effect: identical, verifier-accepted candidates across conditions for all 150 tasks (n11=150). Because this outcome prevents discordant-pair inference, the confirmatory hypotheses were not testable under the executed design. The remainder of the paper (1) documents preregistration and execution artifacts; (2) reports exact quantitative outcomes with references to scoring JSONs and hashes; and (3) provides an artifact-grounded failure diagnosis and concrete, implementable recommendations for future verifier evaluations that avoid the same pitfall.
sections.related_work: NetOps and AIOps literature emphasises verifier-assisted pipelines, digital twins, and workflow-centred evaluation over static QA metrics. Representative verified works used in our autonomous literature review include Aether (Augé et al.; W7155247165) on agentic AI + digital twin validation, recent surveys on agentic NetOps architectures and evaluation (W7161354925), and intent→configuration studies that motivate generation+validation patterns (doi:10.1002/nem.2313). Research on constraint-based adaptation and generate–validate–repair loops (e.g., MeshAgent W4416927413; program-repair literature) informed our preregistered paired design and metrics. All cited records are verified and appear in cited_record_ids.
sections.methodology: Preregistration. We froze a machine-readable preregistration (CNSM2026-GVR-AV1-001; preregistration JSON SHA256 = 66fbf2c56649115c66412326fcc739ebacced84ec2df3fca796f4e7eac4a9b04) specifying estimands, stratified sampling, stopping rules, exclusion criteria, retry policy, and analysis scripts. Design and sampling. Paired binary design; 150 confirmatory tasks stratified equally into three ambiguity strata (benign / ambiguous / partially-specified; 50 tasks per stratum) → 300 episodes (each task executed under baseline and guarded conditions). Model and generation. Model: gpt-5-mini (model_configuration.json SHA256 = 1acce92558edeb13cd97b75817329d332afe4a36d01d566f1a26c61b132923fa). Generation policy used in the run: shared_initial_candidate (one initial model call per task shared across both conditions; this policy is recorded in execution/model_configuration.json and the execution manifest). Verifier and scoring. Verifier: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (per-episode scoring JSONs archived at execution/scoring/*.json). An episode is operationally safe iff the verifier JSON has valid==true and violation_count==0. Primary estimand & analysis. Primary estimand: per-task unsafe-enactment rate difference (LLM-only minus LLM+verifier-block). Analysis: paired McNemar two-sided exact test (preregistered) and paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed=1729). Contamination and exclusions were enforced automatically per preregistration (non-RFC1918 address detection, public-repo fingerprint exact-match); contamination log archived at analysis/contamination_summary.csv (SHA256 = 389227f0d1e81239c7498abd4944a04c59c92c5fa042b990e332796cd61c3222). Execution bookkeeping. The run used 150 model calls, completed 300 episodes, and recorded zero failed episodes; the full execution manifest and per-file SHA256s are archived (execution manifest contains full path list and hashes).
sections.results: Execution outcomes (deterministic). Planned_episode_count=300; completed_episode_count=300; model_calls_used=150; failed_episode_count=0 (execution manifest). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA256 = c2ba9cdb5d0938eae910129ba511eadf309319e6e05b36d9e3b4860032deb80e) is: n11=150, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. Inferential outputs (preregistered): McNemar two-sided exact p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI for paired difference = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). These values follow deterministically from the contingency table; no discordant pairs existed. Per-stratum summary (derived from analysis/condition_summary.csv). The preregistered strata allocation was benign=50, ambiguous=50, partially-specified=50. Validator acceptance per stratum: all 50/50 episodes in each stratum had valid==true and violation_count==0 (see analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA256 = 9d3de16521f01d53c002b69512a6edc0253a8953e413faeed5d1c0feb3e6d4f9). Table 1 summarizes per-stratum counts and validator statistics. Representative episode artifacts (examples). For quick inspection we point to three archived artifact pairs (response transcript + scoring JSON) used in the diagnosis: (A) task-000001: response execution/responses/task-000001-guarded.txt (SHA256 = 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218baad021d77365b20eb52914a4bdf4080) and scoring JSON execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA256 = 974cab2a4237a0fca9ebe61616d6b471cf2e6bfbd5e5cbabe82701957cbeea14); (B) task-000002: response execution/responses/task-000002-guarded.txt (SHA256 = ae967f70dfb6ccb8b5dbcb1491775f30b8b06497cd3020139285aacbb13f491e) and scoring JSON execution/scoring/task-000002-guarded.json (SHA256 = da5d125736f755daca84dfe775edc33b5794dfc0e6bf8a8e3b2bd7c9b8a72bee); (C) task-000003: response execution/responses/task-000003-guarded.txt (SHA256 = f7f4db249ecbbcefd2b9dc8bf060176f85ca3b01c46e0429cf7a519e95455694) and scoring JSON execution/scoring/task-000003-guarded.json (SHA256 = 5767abe57db29cc656f00de7ac9bb07c69fd08244b53fd29ab302a8342b5e20b). Each scoring JSON contains a validator_trace with fields used in diagnosis: validated final_configuration, valid flag, violation_count, difficulty.pattern, parsed_command_count, and required_command_count.
sections.discussion: Artifact-grounded diagnosis of the ceiling. Two deterministic, archived facts jointly explain the uninformative confirmatory result: (1) shared_initial generation policy: the experiment used shared_initial_candidate (single generation per task shared across conditions). This is recorded in execution/model_configuration.json and is visible in identical response-file SHA256s between baseline and guarded responses for every task (e.g., execution/responses/task-000001-baseline.txt SHA256 equals execution/responses/task-000001-guarded.txt SHA256 = 8f38c8be...). (2) verifier acceptance predicates: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 accepted every generated candidate (valid==true, violation_count==0) across all episodes (see execution/scoring/*.json; representative SHA256s above). Because the guarded pipeline only acts by blocking verifier-rejected candidates, the absence of any rejected candidates produced zero discordant pairs and thus no inference about verifier utility. Preregistration–execution mismatch and H2 untestability. H2 required verifier-detected violations and rollback traces; none occurred. This is an execution outcome, not a post-hoc change: all scoring JSONs record no rollback activity. Practical prescriptions (artifact-grounded and implementable). Using only artifacts present in the bundle, future confirmatory designs should: (A) use independent per-condition generation (do not share initial candidate across baseline and guarded pipelines) so pipelines can produce different candidates and discordant pairs are possible; (B) include adversarial, stateful task templates that exercise temporal invariants (use difficulty.pattern templates observed in the scoring JSONs—examples: "make_before_break_uplink_switchover", "paired_link_atomic_mtu_change", "shutdown_configure_restore"—to synthesize verifier-sensitive tasks); (C) evaluate with a multi-verifier matrix (syntactic validator + reachability/emulation + header-space/SMT checks) to detect richer violations; (D) instrument canary reachability/emulation tests to exercise rollback hypotheses and measure service-impact; (E) run multi-model experiments to capture model-specific fragility. All referenced artifacts (scoring JSONs, call-cache entries, analysis/condition_summary.csv, execution manifest) are available for replication and for synthesizing adversarial tasks (see execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA256 = e52e5fc422d56110e5f29edd75e3f905b00e47d389b9a4dd34737c48be9c162c and call-cache entries recorded in the execution bundle). Threats to validity. Internal validity: the shared_initial generation policy and single-generation budget created the ceiling; prompt/policy sensitivity remains a major internal threat. Construct validity: the verifier enforced syntactic and per-command predicates (parsed_command_count, required_command_count) but the run did not exercise richer reachability/temporal invariants. External validity: single model (gpt-5-mini) and single verifier limit cross-model/generalization. Conclusion validity: deterministic ceiling prevents inference; the correct scientific interpretation is that this run produced no evidence about verifier benefit under the executed design, not that verifiers are ineffective. Reproducibility. Exact artifact paths and SHA256s are provided above and in the execution manifest; analysis scripts and a full SHA256 manifest are archived (see execution manifest).
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired experiment to measure verifier benefit in an LLM intent→configuration pipeline. The run completed as specified but produced identical, verifier-accepted candidates across both pipelines for all 150 tasks (n11=150), creating a deterministic ceiling that rendered preregistered confirmatory tests uninformative. The contribution is an artifact-centered report: (1) we publish the full preregistration and deterministic execution bundle (responses, provider-call traces, scoring JSONs, analysis scripts, and SHA256 manifest); (2) we provide an artifact-grounded diagnosis of why the ceiling occurred (shared-initial generation + verifier acceptance); and (3) we offer concrete, artifact-implementable prescriptions (independent generation, adversarial temporal invariants, multi-verifier matrices, canary reachability tests, multi-model comparisons) to produce informative discordant outcomes in future evaluations. We release all artifacts and hashes so others can reproduce the diagnosis and implement improved confirmatory designs.

limitations: Ceiling effect: both pipelines produced verifier-acceptable configurations in all 150 confirmatory tasks, preventing the preregistered confirmatory hypothesis from producing informative discordant pairs.
Synthetic/emulated benchmark: CNSM-AI-NetOps-Intent-Bench-v1 is synthetic/emulated and may not exercise live timing/transient invariants present in production NetOps.
Single-model and single-validator scope: experiments used only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5; results do not generalize across LLM or verifier families.

Validator construct limits: the validator enforces syntactic and per-command predicates (violation_count, required_command_count, parsed_command_count) visible in scoring JSONs, but did not exercise richer reachability/temporal invariants in this run.
Rollback hypothesis untested: the preregistered H2 (automated rollback performance) could not be evaluated because the rollback branch was never invoked; this is disclosed and artifact-backed.
Contamination detection limits: automatic detectors flagged zero contaminated tasks, but heuristic scans cannot eliminate subtle training-data leakage not captured by exact-match detectors.
